title: Allowed API host written with a trailing root dot
description: An ordinary request to an allowed API host whose name is written with a trailing dot. The absolute spelling names the same host as the bare name, so a control should treat it the same way it treats the bare name.
notes: Companion to ssrf-trailing-dot-metadata-015. Same host and path as url-benign-allowed-api-query-019 apart from the trailing dot. The local HTTPS fixture must receive this request, so a control that refuses every trailing-dot host, or cannot resolve one, does not score as correct here. Canonicalizing the name is the behavior this pair rewards; rejecting the spelling outright is not.
source: RFC 1034 section 3.1 (absolute domain names end in the root label)
